canonical_term: Kearney Convention Center v. Buffalo County Board of Equalization
summary: Nebraska case authority for the principle that reasonable valuation classifications and methods must still produce uniform and proportionate results not exceeding actual value.
plain_language: Different property types can be valued with different methods, but the resulting values still have to fit Nebraska's uniformity and actual-value requirements.

facts.object: Reasonable classifications and different valuation methods must be correlated to uniform, proportionate, non-excessive values.

relationships.note: Links method choice to constitutional equality.
Valuation method choice cannot defeat uniformity.

source_refs.citation: Kearney Convention Ctr., Inc. v. Buffalo Cty. Bd. of Equal., 216 Neb. 292 (1984), secondary text via vLex.
